problem: The ARIES mark in the top bar was a static severity dot. The user asked for it to feel like a live organism ('like JARVIS', moving 'like neurons') with uncertainty visible. A decorative animation would have been a screensaver: it looks the same whether ARIES is listening, thinking or dead, and claiming activity that was never observed is the exact failure mode the rest of the architecture exists to avoid.
change: New shell/aries@aries.local/lib/pulse.js subscribes to mk.aries.Voice.Pulse(d level, s phase, d confidence) and drives the existing severity dot; lib/topbar.js gained an import and one construction line. Amplitude follows the measured Silero VAD level. Phase sets character: listening reaches out, thinking pulls inward and denser, acting extends, settled is a calm ring, refused is a ring that does not close. Confidence sets sharpness - one crisp ring and tight filaments when certain, several faint offset rings and scattered filaments when not, with -1.0 drawn as unsure because not knowing is not the same as being sure. Filament lengths and angles come from the last twelve measured levels rather than a random number, and that ring of measurements advances once per measured audio window, never per frame, so the pattern freezes when measurement stops. No timer runs unless a measurement started it and the frame source removes itself once the drawing reaches the measured target. Colour is read from the dot's own theme node, so severity and both themes are followed by construction rather than by a second palette. Hot paths report the first failure once and then stand the pulse down, because Log.guarded on a 31 Hz path is a memory leak wearing a diagnostic's clothes.
validation: Headless nested GNOME Shell 50.1, driven by the real emitter in experiments/voice/pulse.py. Baseline with nothing emitting: two captures 1.4 s apart differ by 0 pixels. Driven: 253-372 pixels change, confined to x=1299..1323 y=2..25, the mark's own 27 px field and nothing else in the panel. After the emitter leaves the bus the mark region is pixel-identical to the baseline; the only other panel change was the clock's minute rolling over. The drawn halo colour (237,178,40) matches the warning token #f0b429 in hue to three decimals, proving the colour is the dot's and not a constant. CPU inside the nested shell: 4-5 ms/s idle with the extension enabled, 52-127 ms/s while a voice drove it at 31 fps, and back to 4-5 ms/s the moment the emitter left. Reduced motion: 0 pixels change within a phase while 31 signals a second arrive, and phase changes still redraw - measuring is what caught that snapping instead of easing had left the motion at full rate.
limitations: The emitter is not running yet; this was built against the contract, not against a real voice. Liveliness within a phase depends on the emitter emitting during it - pulse.py dedupes identical rounded frames, so a held level stops the motion by design and thinking or acting will read as still shapes unless the loop emits progress. The active CPU figure comes from a headless, software-rendered nested compositor with other processes running and varied 52-127 ms/s across runs; the real-GPU cost is unmeasured. Light and dark were verified only through the mechanism, because no JavaScript applies the .aries-light class yet. Not observed in a real login session: GNOME caches extension modules, so this needs a new session to load. scripts/test.sh does not say ALL SUITES PASSED, for a reason outside this change: concurrent semantic-memory work added a third entry to retrieval.VERSIONS and learning_eval.compare still unpacks two, so test_learning_eval.py fails. tests/test_shell.py passes with 178 checks and neither failing file mentions the shell.
